bibliographic.title: From Documents to Decisions: Enterprise-Grade LLM Systems for Zero-Hallucination, Attributed Generation, and Regulatory Alignment
bibliographic.authors: Yenjou Wang; Chihtan Cheng; Jia-Wei Chang
bibliographic.citation_apa: Wang, Y., Cheng, C., & Chang, J.-W. (2026). From documents to decisions: Enterprise-grade LLM systems for zero-hallucination, attributed generation, and regulatory alignment. Computer Modeling in Engineering & Sciences. https://doi.org/10.32604/cmes.2026.080888

methodology.method_family: systematic review with proposed risk-controlled architecture
methodology.study_design: narrative/systematic review of enterprise LLM technologies plus conceptual architecture proposal
methodology.sector: enterprise AI across regulated domains including finance and healthcare
methodology.technology_context: enterprise LLM systems; document perception; RAG; hybrid RAG-KG; multi-agent coordination; OCR; attribution evaluation; risk-controlled data flywheel

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a 2026 peer-reviewed review focused on enterprise-grade LLM governance, traceability, accountability, RAG, and regulatory alignment in high-risk contexts. It strongly matches governance, audit, compliance, and regulated-domain dimensions, but conversational governance is only peripheral via contrast with consumer chatbots rather than being the central object of study.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial excerpts were provided; full review methods, coverage, and conversational relevance need confirmation from the complete text.

appraisal.notes: Clear enterprise-governance objective and proposed architecture are evident, but the provided excerpt does not document full review search strategy, inclusion criteria, or systematic synthesis procedures in enough detail for stronger methodological appraisal.

cerqual.explanation: The text coherently links enterprise LLM deployment to traceability, accountability, and regulatory alignment, but available evidence is limited to introductory sections and does not establish strong conversational-governance specificity or complete review methodology.

coding.theme: Enterprise-grade LLM governance for regulated decision support

synthesis.main_claim: The main obstacle to enterprise LLM adoption is not isolated model capability but the structural gap between fragmented technical modules and the need for high-reliability, governable decision-making in regulated contexts.
synthesis.contribution: The paper reviews enterprise-relevant LLM technologies and proposes a risk-controlled data flywheel architecture integrating perception, reasoning, verification, and governance layers to convert reasoning outputs into observable risk signals and support traceability, accountability, and sustainable optimization.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not fully specify review methodology, corpus scope, or explicit limitations; conversational governance is referenced only indirectly.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for enterprise LLM governance architectures, regulatory alignment, traceability, attribution, RAG-based control, and post-deployment risk monitoring; not as central evidence for conversational governance unless broader review scope treats enterprise decision-support systems as in scope.
